form_description:
This JSON object follows the JSON Schema Draft 7 standard. It tells RJSF what fields to collect, their data types, and validation rules.

type: "object": Defines the root of the form as a single object containing multiple fields.

required: An array listing the fields that must be filled out before the form can be submitted (name, description, etc.). RJSF will automatically add asterisks (*) to these labels.

properties: This is the core dictionary where every form field is defined.

boundary:

Uses enum: This tells RJSF to render a "Select" dropdown or "Radio" buttons instead of a free-text box.

C4 Context: This is a critical architectural distinction. "Internal" actors sit inside the Enterprise Boundary (like employees), while "External" actors sit outside (like customers).

actorType:

Purpose: Distinguishes a human (Person) from an automated external system (Software System). In C4, a "User" is usually a human, but sometimes you need to model a "Bot" or "External Cron Job" that initiates actions.

authentication:

Purpose: Adds security context to the actor. Knowing if a user is "Anonymous" vs "SSO Authenticated" changes the security boundary requirements in the diagram.
